citation.authors: Chiba N, Minamisawa T, Matsuda Y, Fujimoto T
citation.title: Kyphotic Posture Reduces Respiratory Efficiency During Walking and Running

population.description: Ten healthy young men (Methods: 'Ten healthy young men'), each measured in both postures (paired design). No age, height or body mass is printed (only 'young'), so age_years and bmi are null. Screening is not described beyond the paper's word 'healthy'.

protocols.name: walk_4kmh
protocols.description: Walking at 4 km/h, 0% grade, on a rehabilitation treadmill, neutral posture (support belt), Methods and Table 2. No meal and the fed state is not stated (norm_center start). Level from the measured mass-specific VO2 of the neutral condition, 12.5 mL/kg/min (Table 2, VO2/W, 4 km/h; Results): level = (12.5 - 3.7) / 31.7 = 0.2776. Speed was ramped to the target then held for 2 min; the ramp is not printed, so minute 0 is taken as the start of the constant speed, with the activity on for minutes 0 to 2; the sample is the final 60 s (minutes 1 to 2).

protocols.name: run_10kmh
protocols.description: Running at 10 km/h, 0% grade, on a rehabilitation treadmill, neutral posture (support belt), Methods and Table 2. No meal and the fed state is not stated (norm_center start). Level from the measured mass-specific VO2 of the neutral condition, 33.9 mL/kg/min (Table 2, VO2/W, 10 km/h; Results): level = (33.9 - 3.7) / 31.7 = 0.9527 (below 1.0, no extrapolation). Speed was ramped to the target then held for 2 min; the ramp is not printed, so minute 0 is taken as the start of the constant speed, with the activity on for minutes 0 to 2; the sample is the final 60 s (minutes 1 to 2).

left_out.what: Kyphotic (simulated kyphotic) posture: every kyphotic-column value of Table 2 (RR, VO2, VCO2, RER, VE, ETCO2, ETO2, VD/VT and the rest) and the kyphotic-minus-neutral differences with their CIs (Table 2, Results); the model has no posture input

Standing-at-rest values of the neutral posture: RR 15.6 ± 3.3 breaths/min, VO2 309.0 ± 22.6 mL/min and VCO2 261.3 ± 24.5 mL/min (Table 2, Standing rows); the paper's rest is standing on the treadmill, not seated or supine, and its length is not printed
